title: Citation rate
content: Citation rate is the percentage of sampled answers that cite a specified page or domain, with a domain counted once per answer.

meta.why: Citation rate measures how often you appear across the answers you sampled, which is why a single answer with five links to your domain still counts once.
meta.example: If 6 of 20 usable answers cite your domain, its citation rate is 30%, even when some of those answers link to it more than once.
meta.check: Divide the answers citing your domain by all usable sampled answers and multiply by 100, then keep the prompts, engines, dates, and failed runs in the report.
meta.limitation: We use this formula as our own reporting convention, and vendors may calculate citation rate differently. The sample covers the prompts we tested, which is a small slice of all AI searches.
meta.sources: Ahrefs: AI visibility metrics | https://help.ahrefs.com/en/articles/15501968-ai-visibility-metrics | Vendor documentation
